name: Bitcast
gpu_evidence: min_compute.yml:14 (miner spec lists only cpu: 2 / ram: 4, no gpu section; no CUDA/torch/nvidia hits anywhere in repo)
notes: YouTube creator-economy subnet. Miner publishes videos against briefs; validators read YouTube Analytics via OAuth. Software setup is light (Dockerfile + docker-compose at root, requirements.txt, bittensor 10.3.0), but mining requires real YouTube accounts and OAuth wiring (up to 5 accounts per miner). Only 4 active miners, near-zero burn.

name: Verathos
notes: Miner serves inference and must run on a 24GB+ NVIDIA GPU (CUDA 12.8+, 32GB RAM, 100GB disk); validator explicitly gpu required: false (min_compute.yml:43). install.sh + pyproject + pm2 ecosystem example. 55 active miners, 41% burn - the most contested subnet in this batch.

name: Albedo
gpu_evidence: docs/MINING.md:7 and docs/MINING.md:9 (miner must fine-tune a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model); pyproject.toml:32 (vllm==0.23.0), pyproject.toml:27 (torch==2.11.0)
notes: King-of-the-hill LLM subnet. Miner fine-tunes a 35B-A3B Qwen checkpoint, uploads to HuggingFace/Hippius, commits an on-chain reveal; must beat the incumbent king by a 3% margin. No min_compute.yml and no explicit miner VRAM figure - the eval side documents multi-GPU hosts (docs/eval-service-status.md:34 requires free_gpu_count >= 8) but that is validator infra, not the miner. Highest registration cost in batch (~1.02 TAO), 5 active miners.

name: NeverPlayAlone
gpu_evidence: docs/miner.md:9-14 (Requirements section lists only Python 3.10+, a registered wallet, and Node.js; docs/miner.md:25 states miners do not even need Docker to submit). No cuda/nvidia/torch hits anywhere in the repo.
notes: Minecraft agent subnet, winner-take-all. Miner writes a Node.js agent, tars it, and uploads via the npacli CLI; validators run it in a sandboxed no-internet container against NPA-Bench. Zero infra burden, but agent quality is the whole game. Only 1 active miner and prune_rank 20 - very thin.

name: BASE
gpu_evidence: docs/external-miner/prism.md:35 (evaluation runs on operator-rented Lium GPU pods, not on miner hardware); docs/external-miner/prism.md:19 caps submitted models at 350M parameters
notes: Rust control plane (rust-toolchain 1.96.0, cargo workspace) plus docker-compose. Miner must deploy a measured Phala/dstack CVM with digest-pinned base-agent and certify each epoch via a loopback attest-helper - confidential-VM attestation is the hard part, not GPU. Highest operational ceremony in the batch.

name: ConnitoAI
gpu_evidence: docs/miner-faq/faq.md:249 ("A 24 GB consumer GPU (3090 / 4090) is a reasonable minimum"); docs/miner-faq/architecture.md:34 (miner = one GPU); docs/miner-faq/miner-config.md:140 (single-GPU only)
notes: Collaborative MoE LLM training across distributed expert groups. Miner runs a single-GPU training loop (connito/miner/train.py, torch, device=cuda per pyproject.toml:77); validator ships a nvidia/cuda:12.4.1 Docker image needing NVIDIA Container Toolkit and a 40GB A100/H100. Also needs an HF_TOKEN with access to the gated nvidia/Nemotron-CC-Math-v1 dataset. Stalest repo in batch (last commit 2026-07-31), 25% burn.

name: Nodexo
gpu_evidence: README.md:42 (miner minimum = Ubuntu/Debian GPU host, supported NVIDIA GPU, working nvidia-smi); docs/SUPPORTED_GPUS.md:15 (lowest accepted model: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24 GB)
notes: GPU rental marketplace with zkGEMM proofs. Miner setup hard-stops unless the detected GPU model/count matches calibrated timing policy - only H100 80GB, A100 80GB (SXM4/PCIe), RTX A6000 48GB and RTX 4090 24GB accepted today. Also needs Docker, a public API port and a rental TCP port range reachable from validators/renters. Cheapest registration in batch (0.0005 TAO) but the hardware gate is the real cost.

name: Minos
gpu_evidence: min_compute.yml:24 (miner gpu required: False - "GATK and DeepVariant can run on CPU"), min_compute.yml:25 (min_vram: 0)
notes: Genomics variant-calling subnet. CPU-only path is explicitly supported; GPU only optionally accelerates the DeepVariant template (recommended_vram: 8, min_compute.yml:26). Docker is mandatory (min_compute.yml:56) with ~7GB of biocontainer images (samtools + one of gatk/deepvariant/bcftools), 8GB RAM min, 60GB SSD with 3000+ IOPS. pm2 + install.sh scaffolding. Registration 0.99 TAO, 20 active miners, prune_rank 110 (weakest prune position in batch).

name: minotaur
gpu_evidence: docs/miner/quickstart.md:9 (only prerequisite listed is Docker, required for git-based submission screening). No gpu/cuda/nvidia/vram hits anywhere in README.md, docs/, or requirements.txt.
notes: DEX/intent-solving subnet. Miner writes a Python Solving Engine and submits a git repo; validators run 3-stage sandboxed screening (Docker build + import) then benchmark against the champion, with hidden shadow cases. A local testnet reproduces the full screening/benchmark pipeline for iteration. Highest burn in batch (80%), only 1 active miner, prune_rank 5 - registration is 0.99 TAO into a near-empty, heavily-burning subnet.

name: SOMA
gpu_evidence: README.md:62-64 ("All a miner needs to participate is: A working algorithm that solves the active MCP task; A registered hotkey on netuid 114" - platform handles orchestration and evaluation). README.md:47 hardware minimums (4 CPU cores / 16GB RAM / 500GB SSD, no GPU) apply to validators.
notes: MCP-server subnet run as competitions; current competition is Agent CoT compression. Miner writes an algorithm and uploads it to the central platform via miner/upload_miner_with_openrouter_key.py (needs an OpenRouter key); no local serving infra. torch>=2 appears only in mcp_platform/requirements.txt (the platform component), not in the miner path. Lowest setup burden in batch, but heavy central-platform dependency and only 3 active miners.
